sections.heading: Opening Cash Position and Liquidity Buffer
sections.body: As of 30 June 2026, consolidated cash and cash equivalents totaled USD 412.7 million, held across 14 operating accounts in North America and EMEA. The approved minimum liquidity buffer for Q3 2026 is USD 275 million, representing approximately 2.4 months of projected operating cash outflows under base-case assumptions. After scheduled debt service of USD 38.5 million in July and forecast capital expenditures of USD 52 million for the quarter, available liquidity remains above the board-mandated threshold. Daily cash concentration to the primary USD header account at Horizon National Bank continues to operate without exception.

sections.heading: Short-Term Funding Sources
sections.body: The company maintains access to USD 600 million in committed revolving credit facilities, split between a USD 400 million syndicated revolver (maturing May 2029) and a USD 200 million bilateral line with Crestmark Bank (maturing December 2027). As of the reporting date, USD 185 million is drawn under the syndicated facility and USD 40 million under the bilateral line, resulting in total utilization of 37.5% of committed capacity. Average all-in borrowing cost for Q2 was SOFR + 165 bps, equating to 6.14% on a blended basis. Treasury intends to reduce revolver drawings by approximately USD 50 million by late August through excess operating cash and targeted working capital collections.

sections.heading: Commercial Paper and Intercompany Funding
sections.body: The EUR 150 million commercial paper program remains undrawn at quarter start, providing supplemental flexibility for European subsidiaries. Intercompany loans totaling USD 96 million are outstanding from the U.S. parent to subsidiaries in Germany and the Netherlands, primarily to fund seasonal inventory builds. These balances are expected to normalize by September as receivables collections accelerate. No covenant restrictions are currently triggered under any intercompany or external borrowing arrangements.

sections.heading: EUR)
sections.body: USD would impact quarterly EBITDA by an estimated USD 3.1 million post-hedge.

sections.heading: Liquidity Stress Scenarios and Mitigation
sections.body: Under the moderate stress scenario (15% revenue contraction and 20-day DSO extension), projected quarter-end liquidity declines to USD 301 million, remaining above the minimum buffer. In the severe scenario (25% revenue decline, partial revolver covenant tightening, and 150 bps rate shock), liquidity would fall to USD 244 million absent corrective action. Mitigation measures include suspension of non-essential capital expenditures (USD 28 million deferrable), temporary hiring freeze, and accelerated drawdown of the remaining undrawn revolver capacity. Based on these levers, treasury projects restoration of liquidity to at least USD 285 million within 30 days of stress onset.

structure.heading: Q3 2026 Cash Position and Short‑Term Funding Plan (Minimum Buffer Protection)
text_content: **Q3 2026 Cash Position and Short‑Term Funding Plan (Minimum Buffer Protection)**

As of 30 June 2026 the Group's cash and cash equivalents total USD 182.4m, held across operating accounts, overnight placements, and short‑term liquid instruments. The Treasury maintains a minimum daily liquidity floor of USD 60.0m to ensure operational continuity; this floor represents 32.9% of the June 30 cash balance. Daily cash reporting and end‑of‑day reconciliations are performed by Treasury operations with automated alerts to the CFO and liquidity committee when projected end‑of‑day balances approach a 10% buffer above the floor. Short‑duration allocation and overnight sweep arrangements prioritise preservation of principal and immediate access while maximising marginal yield consistent with the floor. Investment counterparties are limited to rated institutions.

The primary short‑term funding event in Q3 is the USD 40.0m commercial paper maturity on 15 August 2026. With the current cash position and the USD 60.0m floor, the Group has immediate headroom of USD 122.4m, equivalent to 3.06x coverage of that maturity. Treasury's execution plan targets a decision by 10 August 2026 on whether to refinance via the CP programme, execute a private placement with eligible counterparties, or utilise committed back‑stop instruments. Pricing and tenor will be negotiated to avoid intraday depletion below the floor. Execution will prioritise cost‑effective rollover while preserving the daily liquidity buffer and maintaining counterparty concentration limits. All actions require treasury committee sign‑off.

Protecting the USD 60.0m minimum daily liquidity floor is governed by a three‑tier escalation framework and clear operational controls. Any projection indicating end‑of‑day cash below the floor triggers immediate escalation to the CFO and CEO and prompt execution of contingency steps; projections within 5% above the floor (USD 63.0m) prompt pre‑emptive conservation measures. Contingency options include suspension of discretionary outflows (capital expenditure, non‑essential vendor payments), acceleration of receivables collection, and temporary utilisation of intraday liquidity mechanisms. Treasury will provide daily exception reports and a consolidated weekly status to the Audit and Risk Committee; remediation steps require treasury committee approval and documented rollback criteria. Quarterly testing is mandatory, documented.

structure.heading: Credit Facility Utilisation, FX Exposure Management, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios (Q3 2026 Readiness)
text_content: **Credit Facility Utilisation, FX Exposure Management, and Liquidity Stress Scenarios (Q3 2026 Readiness)**

As of 30 Jun 2026 the syndicated revolving credit facility is USD 300.0m with USD 120.0m drawn. Current utilisation of 40.0% supports near‑term working capital and provides a flexible backstop for Q3 cash flow variance. The facility remains in compliance with financial covenants based on the June reporting package; pricing is negotiated quarterly with our lead arrangers and early renewal options are being reviewed to lock margins before anticipated market tightening in late 2026. Treasury will maintain a minimum lender notification lead time of five business days for redraws, and will prioritize bilateral term loans only if syndicate capacity or covenant ratios materially change. All draws require standard documentation.

Q3 2026 forecast flows present a net USD exposure of USD 95.0m and a net EUR exposure of EUR 60.0m. Treasury will apply a layered hedging approach combining forwards, selective purchased options, and intra‑company netting to limit realised volatility. Immediate priority is to hedge 60% of net USD exposure through 3‑ and 6‑month forwards with primary banking counterparties, while EUR exposure will be managed using a staggered forward schedule to mature between August and October 2026. Hedging execution targets a maximum portfolio delta exposure equivalent to a 2.5% adverse rate move; all trades comply with counterparty limits and ISDA documentation. Weekly FX reporting will be reviewed by CFO.

In the combined stress scenario the lowest projected cash balance falls to USD 48.0m on 12 Sep 2026. This outcome triggers the Contingency Liquidity Plan: immediate draw of committed lines where necessary, temporary suspension of non‑critical capex, accelerated receivables collection, and invocation of supplier payment extensions subject to negotiation. Operational trigger thresholds are set such that any projected day with less than USD 55.0m cash within a 14‑day horizon requires executive treasury approval to draw or seek external funding. Stress reporting will be provided daily from 1 September through 30 September 2026 to the CEO and CFO, and relevant actions logged for audit and regulator review. Remediation timelines apply.
